decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 3/round 2: “save links, organise them by topic… through search and filtering.” Response entry 4: “Yes, that captures it.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level scope decision during goal confirmation.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3 asks the client to enter a “link address” and click “Save link.” Response entry 6 confirms the link was saved.
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3 defines exactly three save fields: “link address, a title, and a topic,” omitting description editing before save. Response entry 6 says only that “Three fields still feels quick enough.”
decisions.note: Prototype save form omits the reference-required editable description; the response does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3 provides one singular “topic” field and groups each link beneath that topic. Response entry 6 approves the three-field flow and topic grouping.
decisions.note: Prototype uses a single-category topic model rather than allowing one or more tags; approval does not express awareness of the cardinality difference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 7/round 4 says search looks across “everything at once — the title, the link address, and the topic.” Response entry 8 approves those fields as natural.
decisions.note: Prototype search excludes description and note, both required full-text fields; the client does not mention the omission.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 9/round 5 offers three ways to “narrow the list down to just your ‘Design’ links.” Response entry 10 selects topic buttons.
decisions.note: All offered UI variants implement specific-tag filtering; differences among button, dropdown, and heading controls are equivalent implementation preferences.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 9/round 5 says all versions permit search while a topic is selected. Response entry 10: “Searching while a topic is selected also makes sense.”
decisions.note: Conforming combination of a selected-topic filter with textual search during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 11/round 6 asks the client to add a link “with a topic” and confirms creation of one corresponding group/button. Response entry 12 confirms the singular Travel topic behavior.
decisions.note: Integrated prototype re-presents the single-topic model rather than multi-tag assignment; the response does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 11/round 6 asks whether changing a saved link is needed or “not important for this first version.” Response entry 12 selects the conforming alternative: “I also need to be able to edit a saved link’s address, title, or topic.”
decisions.note: The client selects bookmark editing when offered an alternative that would omit it.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 11/round 6 asks whether removing saved links is needed or not important. Response entry 12: “I also need to… delete links I no longer want.”
decisions.note: The client selects deletion when offered an alternative that would omit it.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 13/round 7 limits editable fields to “address, title, topic.” Response entry 14 approves: “editing the topic moved the link” and “Editing in place feels natural.”
decisions.note: Implemented editing omits description, markdown note, and multi-tag editing; the response does not surface those omissions.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 13/round 7 provides deletion with a confirmation step. Response entry 14 confirms that deletion removed the link and approves confirmation.
decisions.note: Conforming delete behavior; confirmation is an orthogonal safety choice.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 15/round 8 says a bookmark saved without a title displays its URL as the name, rather than collecting the page title. Response entry 16: “Using the address when the title is blank makes sense.”
decisions.note: The blank-title behavior directly establishes that page-title metadata is not automatically collected; the client accepts the fallback without stating the reference expectation.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 17/round 9 states that a link address is required. Response entry 18: “Yes, the address should be required.”
decisions.note: Conforming required-URL decision.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 17/round 9 offers allowing a duplicate or merely pointing out that it is already saved. Response entry 18 supplies the reference behavior: “let me edit the existing bookmark instead of creating a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The client corrects the duplicate-save behavior by requiring convergence on editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 19/round 10 says a repeated address reports the duplicate and opens the existing link for editing. Response entry 20 confirms it “opened the existing bookmark for editing rather than creating another.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised duplicate handling during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 19/round 10 asks the client to confirm that a saved link is clickable and opens properly. Response entry 20 confirms both worked as wanted.
decisions.note: Conforming navigation to the bookmarked URL; URL normalization is an orthogonal enhancement.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12: “You add a link with its address” and “The address is the only thing that’s required.” Response entry 24 says the scope matches the agreement.
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 defines saving as the user adding “its address, a title, and a topic,” with only the address required, carrying forward the URL-as-title fallback from entry 15. Response entry 24 gives general approval.
decisions.note: The locked first-version save workflow lacks automatic collection of title, description, favicon, and preview image; bare scope approval does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 locks the save inputs as address, title, and topic, with no description field. Response entry 24 says the summary matches what was agreed.
decisions.note: The specification omits editing an automatically collected description before or after save; the response is bare approval.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 repeatedly uses singular “a topic” and places each bookmark under one topic heading. Response entry 24 approves the scope as complete.
decisions.note: The specification retains a single topic per bookmark instead of one-or-more tag assignment.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12: a repeated link “opens the existing one to edit instead of piling up copies.” Response entry 24 approves.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save rule at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 limits search matching to “titles, addresses, or topics.” Response entry 24 approves the first-version scope without mentioning description or note search.
decisions.note: Locked search scope excludes the reference-required description and note fields.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 includes “One-click topic buttons” to focus on a topic. Response entry 24 approves.
decisions.note: Conforming specific-topic filtering at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 promises in-place editing, carrying forward entry 13’s explicit editable fields of address, title, and topic. Response entry 24 approves the complete scope.
decisions.note: The locked edit operation still omits description, markdown note, and multi-tag editing.

decisions.evidence: Specification presentation entry 23/round 12 says the user can delete a link with confirmation. Response entry 24 approves.
decisions.note: Conforming deletion decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports passing checks for saving and “the required-address rule.” Response entry 26 accepts the software and specifically includes “saving.”
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision based on the presented behavior; no independent execution is inferred.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports “saving & topic grouping” verified against the singular-topic scenarios agreed earlier. Response entry 26 accepts saving and topic filtering without identifying the absence of multiple tags.
decisions.note: Implementation review retains the divergent single-topic model; acceptance does not express the difference.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports live search verified against the previously agreed title/address/topic behavior. Response entry 26 accepts “searching.”
decisions.note: The implemented search is presented as realizing the earlier limited field set, so description and note remain excluded; the response does not surface this.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports checks for topic buttons, and response entry 26 accepts “topic filtering.”
decisions.note: Conforming topic-filter implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports duplicate handling verified. Response entry 26 specifically accepts “duplicate handling.”
decisions.note: Conforming implementation of duplicate convergence to the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports “in-place editing” verified against the approved address/title/topic scenario. Response entry 26 globally accepts the software as behaving as agreed.
decisions.note: Implementation review preserves the limited edit-field set; the client does not express the omitted description, note, or multi-tag editing.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation entry 25/round 13 reports “delete-with-confirmation” verified. Response entry 26 accepts the software as behaving as agreed.
decisions.note: Conforming deletion implementation review.
